rows.41:ee28:
So maybe it really is true after all, huh.
If that letter was telling the truth, then where did the fortune-teller go once she was released from the job?
I think that old woman is suspicious.
If it's just like the letter says, the fortune-teller must be pretty old.
You can hide your face and body to some extent with makeup and a robe, and places like that keep the lights low, don't they?
You can fake your age pretty easily, you know.
Or maybe you don't age while you're living as a fortune-teller?
Come to think of it, Hirai looks young, you know.
Last holiday, I went with my big sister to visit her in the hospital.
That was the first time I'd ever met Hirai, but according to my sister, she hasn't changed one bit since back then.
She's the same age as my sister, so, um, she should be twenty-three this year, but however you look at her, she looks fifteen or sixteen.
And it's not like she's just trying to look young or anything.
The firmness and texture of her skin are completely different.
So the idea that time stops while you're living as a fortune-teller somehow doesn't seem so wrong to me.
I think lots of people still wish they could never age and never die, but do you think it's really such a good thing?
I mean, what did that letter say?
"Thank you," that's what.
If that fortune-teller had also taken over from some other fortune-teller somewhere, then they all want to be released, even if they have to find someone to take their place.
Then again, once death starts slowly creeping up on them, I bet they start saying
"I want to go back to never aging and never dying"
all over again.
Well, people always want what they can't have.
But if Hirai has turned into an old woman by the time she's released from the job, what will she do?
Will she marry Tanaka after he's turned into an old man?
I mean, sure, her wish would come true that way.
Whether she'd be happy or not is another matter.
It'd be lucky for her if she got released from the job soon, though.
Hmm, if I ever have someone I want to curse, maybe I'll go see her.
Since Hirai's fortunes never come true, the curse would probably be just for show, though...
I recommend her to anyone interested in never aging and never dying.
Okay, that's the end of my story.
But still, the seventh person isn't coming, are they?
I wonder if something happened...{p}
rows.41:10a8c:
Someone like her big brother.
That brother of hers was really cool, apparently.
Dependable, I guess you'd say. He was student council president and stuff.
He was smart, and he had a great personality too.
If he had any flaw, it was that he was soft on his little sister.
That's the kind of person he was.
You can see why Hirai would get so attached to her brother, right?
He was the brother she was proud of.
And Hirai was really beautiful, but...
her personality had a bit of a problem.{p}
